evidence: Quint. 9.4.47: ūna enim syllaba longa pār est duābus brevibus
terms.comment: A syllable is long by nature or by position: nātūrā brevis, tamen positiōne longa (Quint. 1.5.28). To lengthen a vowel or syllable is prōdūcere, to shorten it corripere (Cic. Or. 159; Quint. 1.5.18); to pronounce a vowel long, prōductē prōnūntiāre (Traupman 248; prōductē dīcere, Cic. Or. 159). A long mark is nota longa (Traupman 247).

evidence: Cic. Or. 159: inclitus dīcimus brevī prīmā litterā, īnsānus prōductā (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: nam volucrēs mediā acūtā legam, quia, etsī nātūrā brevis, tamen positiōne longa est
phrases.english: for I shall read volucrēs with the acute on the middle syllable, since though short by nature it is long by position

phrases.latin: sīve cum syllaba correpta prōdūcitur … seu longa corripitur
phrases.english: whether a short syllable is lengthened … or a long one shortened

sources: Lewis & Short: longus · Lewis & Short: produco · Lewis & Short: corripio
